title: PSE&G Demand Response Participation Nearly Doubles as Second Season Concludes

# PSE&G Demand Response Participation Nearly Doubles as Second Season Concludes


## *Nearly 45,000 customers enrolled as programs help reduce electricity demand during critical peak periods*


NEWARK, N.J. – November 17, 2026 – PSE&G's Demand Response programs wrapped up their second season with nearly 45,000 customers enrolled, almost double the approximately 23,000 customers enrolled at the end of the 2025 season.


During PSE&G’s 2026 Demand Response season, which ran from June 1 through Oct. 30, the company called 16 Demand Response events to help reduce electricity use during periods of high demand. During one event this summer, customers reduced demand by 38.15 megawatts (MW), which is the approximate equivalent of taking 18,000 homes off the grid during that one-hour period. The programs were successfully dispatched during each of the five highest PJM grid peak hours, helping reduce electric demand on the regional grid during those critical periods.


“The growth we’ve seen in the program enables more flexibility on the grid during critical peak demand periods,” said Lauren Thomas, vice president, Clean Energy Solutions – Customer Solutions, PSE&G. “With more customers participating, we have a larger pool of resources we can call on when electricity demand is highest, helping reduce pressure on the grid when it matters most.”


Customer participation has grown steadily since PSE&G launched its Demand Response programs. At this same time last year, approximately 23,000 customers and just over 30,000 devices were enrolled. Through the end of October 2026, enrollment had grown to approximately 45,000 customers and 60,000 devices.


PSE&G offers two Demand Response programs: FlexPower and SmartFlex. FlexPower works with eligible smart devices, including smart thermostats, electric vehicles and chargers, and certain electric water heaters to temporarily adjust energy use during scheduled events. Customers can receive a $50 prepaid gift card for each new device type enrolled, plus $25 each year they remain in the program. SmartFlex allows customers to actively reduce electricity use during events, with or without a smart device, and earn $1.25 for every kilowatt-hour of energy saved during an event. Both programs help PSE&G manage demand during periods when electricity use is highest.


The experience gained from managing customer resources through PSE&G’s Demand Response and other customer programs will help inform the company’s continued work to manage peak demand as New Jersey advances its virtual power plant program and other energy management solutions.


Demand Response is also part of PSE&G’s broader efforts to give customers more options to manage when and how they use energy while supporting a more reliable, flexible electric grid. While Demand Response focuses on periods during the year when electricity demand is at its highest,[PSE&G’s Time of Use (TOU) rate](https://landing.pseg.com/TOU) gives customers an option to manage their energy use every day of the year by shifting usage to different times of day.
